page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.2xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by an AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 8 physical cores and 8 vCPUs with a dedicated CPU allocation running at 2.5 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and includes 474 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. Network performance is supported by a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark results indicate average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 12133.14 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5364.0. Single-core performance is relatively weaker, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 930.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1519.88. Memory bandwidth is solid, reaching 473.11 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 116.89 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, though write speeds drop to 50.84 GB/sec. The server performs moderately in database operations, achieving 9.43 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 5269.76 in Passmark database tests. However, it exhibits poor performance in single-threaded decompression and LLM text generation.

The c6gd.2xlarge offers a balanced profile for workloads requiring local, low-latency NVMe storage alongside dedicated ARM-based compute resources. The inclusion of 474 GB of local NVMe SSD storage provides high resource density for applications that require fast temporary storage without the overhead of network-attached volumes. However, the 2 Gbps network baseline and weaker single-threaded performance represent notable tradeoffs. This instance is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, software compilation, and database operations that can leverage the local instance store.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gd.2xlarge is a compute-optimized, ARM-based server powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 16.0 GB of system memory, 474 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, and a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, this instance provides dedicated CPU allocation with no hyperthreading. Benchmark data shows average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 12133.14 and solid memory read bandwidth of up to 473.11 GB/sec. However, single-core performance and single-threaded decompression speeds are relatively weak. The integrated NVMe storage enhances qualitative cost efficiency for data-intensive tasks by eliminating external storage overhead. This server is best suited for multi-threaded workloads, software compilation, static web serving, and database operations that benefit from local high-speed storage.
